newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSL signs vaccine j/v with Astra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSL signs vaccine j/v with Astra.

text.p: Vaccine and blood products manufacturer CSL Ltd said on Wednesday it had signed a joint venture agreement with Sweden's Astra AB to develop a vaccine to treat peptic ulcers and stomach cancers.

CSL said it had been collaborating with the University of New South Wales on the development of a vaccine to treat bacterial infections caused by Helicobacter pylori, recognised as the primary cause of peptic ulcers, and an important factor in certain stomach cancers in humans.
"CSL and Astra, will build on this work to develop a vaccine for treatment of H.pylori infection in humans," CSL said.

"The agreement provides Astra AB with an exclusive licence and global commercial rights to CSL's portfolio of H.pylori intellectual property as well as CSL's extensive immunology and vaccine development expertise," it said.
"CSL will retain a co-exclusive right to market the vaccine in Australia, New Zealand and Indonesia."
CSL said it would make a major commitment to development and commercial scale-up of the H.pylori vaccine with Astra's help.
"The Astra/CSL/UNSW collaboration anticipates having CSL-produced vaccine material available for initial evaluation in humans in approximately two years," CSL said.
"Assuming successful development and regulatory approval, CSL will also construct and operate a facility in Melbourne to produce the Kpylori vaccine for Astra internationally."
CSL Managing Director Brian McNamee said the collaboration would involve many millions of dollars and a large commitment of scientific and manufacturing resources.
"The project offers the potential to yield one of the most exciting, innovative and commercially significant vaccines in many years.
The annual global market for peptic ulcer treatments is currently around US$9 billion, CSL said.
CSL shares closed down ten cents at A$6.40 on Tuesday.
